title: Incremental event schema validator and ingress backpressure proxy
creator: Asha Patil
description: Build a streaming-first ingestion path that performs incremental schema validation without becoming the single point of failure for usage analytics. The design introduces a lightweight ingress proxy that applies adaptive backpressure when downstream validators are saturated and a Wasm-based validation stage that can be hot-swapped with new schema versions. Goals: maintain low ingest latency for valid events, provide graceful degradation for schema evolution, and capture invalid payloads for offline repair.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress proxy enforces soft backpressure and returns 429 when downstream queue > 80% capacity
Wasm-based validator supports pluggable schema versions from the schema registry and can be rotated without restarting the proxy
Invalid events are routed to an S3 quarantine bucket and a sampled stream (1%) is forwarded to a repair pipeline
End-to-end p50 latency for validated events < 60ms, p99 < 250ms at 50k EPS
Automatic metrics emitted to telemetry: validation_rate, invalid_rate_by_schema, validator_queue_depth, backpressure_trips
tasks: Design ingress backpressure algorithm and thresholds
Prototype Wasm validator using existing schema definitions
Implement proxy to forward to validator and Kafka topic fallback
Integrate schema registry API for version discovery
Add quarantine write path to S3 and repair stream to Snowplow reprocess job
Create Grafana dashboards and PagerDuty alerts for validator saturation
comments: 2025-02-13 - Marcus Nguyen: Spike complete. Wasm validation is ~3-4x faster than naive JSON Schema on a single thread for our golden events. Need to benchmark under 50k EPS with batching.
2025-02-20 - Leah Kim (PM): Prioritize soft backpressure (429s) over buffering at proxy to avoid memory blowup in bursty customer traffic. Customers expect timely feedback when events rejected.
2025-02-24 - Omar Velez (SRE): Recommend replication of validator pods across AZs and local in-region S3 quarantine to avoid cross-region writes during incidents.

2025-02-27 - Marcus Nguyen: Implemented initial healthcheck and queue-length metrics. Deployed to staging. Observed validator_queue_depth spike on a malformed schema rollout test; proxy returned 429s as designed.

2025-03-01 - Asha Patil: Design review notes: add schema evolution guide and automated compatibility checker in registry to reduce invalid-rate during rollouts. Also add canary header to bypass backpressure for debug clients.
decisions: Use Wasm for validator runtime to allow polyglot validation modules and hot-swapping without JVM/Go restarts
Ingress proxy will implement soft backpressure (429) with exponential backoff recommendations in response headers
All invalid events are written to a per-customer S3 quarantine with metadata for re-ingestion; a sampled repair stream (1%) forwards to the repair job for triage
Primary message bus remains Kafka for validated events; fallback is a durable S3 write when Kafka is unavailable
rollout_plan: Canary rollout in eu-west-1 staging (10% traffic) -> extended soak (48h) -> us-west-2 canary (25%) -> full rollout. During canaries monitor invalid_rate_by_schema and backpressure_trips; rollback if invalid_rate increases > 5x baseline or p99 latency > 300ms.
notes: Trade-offs considered: synchronous validation provides immediate feedback but risks higher latency; we chose a hybrid approach where minimal validation (required fields, size limits) happens inline and deeper schema checks run in the Wasm stage.
Future work: add an automated schema migration path that can transform old payload variants to the latest schema using wasm transformers and reduce quarantine rates.
Follow-ups: coordinate with SDK team to add retry/backoff guidance and client-side sampling for high-volume sources.
